context: Open Questions: Our work establishes the near-optimal query and time complexity of P ROPERTY T ESTING FOR PATTERN M ATCHING (Problem I.2). Nevertheless, the extensions give rise to several interesting open questions. We are not aware how to generalize our adaptive algorithm (Theorem I.7) to the tolerant version (Problem I.10) or the reporting version (Problem I.11 with k ′ = 0). In both cases, we suggest considering n = m + O(m/k) e first; in that setting, our algorithm runs in O(m/k) time (see Figure 1), and many of its steps simplify (see the e O(∆ + n/k)-complexity version in Section II-D). • In [4, Theorem 10.5], Problem I.10 is solved with gap k/k ′ = 1 + ϵ (for an arbitrarily small constant ϵ > 0) in 1/3−o(1)  e n/k ϵ sublinear running time O . Unfortunately, our new techniques increase the gap by a factor of 2, and thus they offer improvements only for sufficiently large constant gaps. It remains open to improve upon the results of [4] for smaller gaps. • In general, the time complexity of Problem I.10 with k/k ′ = 1 + ϵ is wide open. Fact I.3 can be easily modified to solve this version at the price of a poly( 1ϵ )factor overhead in the query complexity, so an improved unconditional lower bound is beyond the scope of the current techniques. Still, one can hope for lower bounds conditioned on fine-grained complexity hypotheses. • In the second extension, we ask the algorithm to output a set A of candidate occurrences such that Occk′ (P, T ) ⊆ A ⊆ Occk (P, T ). Intuitively, this requires distinguishing HD(P, T [i. .i + m)) ≤ k ′ and HD(P, T [i. .i + m)) > k for each candidate i ∈ [0. .n − m] rather than just for mini∈[0. .n−m] HD(P, T [i. .i + m)). We adjust our non-adaptive algorithms to handle extensions at the price of small overheads in the time and query complexities. The multiplicative overhead for the tolerant version is O(1) if k ′ = O(k/ log n), and no(1) if k ′ = o(k).
